directAnswer: St. Sixtus III was a Roman priest who served as pope from 432 to 440. He supported the reconciliation of Cyril of Alexandria with John of Antioch after the Council of Ephesus and built the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore, whose mosaics still bear his name. His feast day is March 28.

sections.h2: Santa Maria Maggiore and the Lateran Baptistery
paras: Sixtus is best remembered as a builder. On the Esquiline Hill he erected the great basilica now called Santa Maria Maggiore, one of the four major basilicas of Rome. The mosaics of its triumphal arch, honoring Mary and the infancy of Christ, carry the inscription Xystus episcopus plebi Dei, Bishop Sixtus to the people of God.

The church is widely seen as a celebration of the Council of Ephesus, which had affirmed Mary as Mother of God the year before his election. Sixtus also rebuilt the Lateran baptistery in its octagonal form, with verse inscriptions on the meaning of baptism that are still preserved.

The Council of Ephesus had left Cyril of Alexandria and John of Antioch at odds. In 433, they agreed on a joint statement of faith, the Formula of Union, and Sixtus welcomed the reconciliation in letters to both.

Earlier in life, as a Roman priest, Sixtus had been thought sympathetic to Pelagius, but he later opposed the movement, and Augustine wrote to him praising his firmness. As pope, he refused to readmit Julian of Eclanum to communion. He also defended Rome's rights over the churches of Illyricum. Sixtus died on August 18, 440, while the deacon Leo, his eventual successor, was away on a mission in Gaul.

keyFacts: Built Santa Maria Maggiore; its arch mosaics bear his name
Welcomed the 433 reconciliation between Cyril of Alexandria and John of Antioch

faqs.question: Did Pope Sixtus III build Santa Maria Maggiore?
faqs.answer: Yes. The present basilica was built under Sixtus III, and the mosaic inscription on its triumphal arch names him as the bishop who dedicated it to the people of God.

faqs.question: How was Pope Sixtus III connected to the Council of Ephesus?
faqs.answer: He became pope the year after the council, celebrated its teaching on Mary through Santa Maria Maggiore, and supported the reconciliation of the Alexandrian and Antiochene churches in 433.
